battle.name: 沙那圍城戰 (570年)
battle.brief: 公元570年，阿克蘇姆王國（埃塞俄比亞）將軍阿布拉哈為逐走薩珊波斯在也門的駐軍，率軍圍困也門高原都城沙那；波斯使者馬茲卡在場遊說，圍城數月不能破，進攻方遂轉而北上攻擊麥加。卡面羅馬標槍並未隨軍而至，但阿克蘇姆步兵在牆下所投的短矛與羅馬標槍同屬破盾投槍的技術路線。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 沙那圍城戰是六世紀末阿克蘇姆王國與薩珊波斯爭奪也門的諸役之一，交戰地點是也門高原的都城沙那。圍城方是阿克蘇姆王國（埃塞俄比亞）派出的遠征軍，由貴族出身、久經軍旅的將領阿布拉哈統率，麾下有本國步兵與騎兵、受雇於其的拜占庭風格雇傭兵、希木葉殘部以及阿拉伯部落的傭兵；指揮系統以王命與將軍軍令為樞紐，營地與序列帶有羅馬式軍營的傳統，甲士、象隊與帳列為核心。守城方是薩珊波斯在也門的駐軍，由薩珊任命的也門總督率領，麾下有波斯籍與阿拉伯籍的軍人、希木葉當地民兵，以及城內基督徒與猶太社群的武裝壯丁；波斯方面的指揮依薩珊的省區體制，由總督統轄城防與外圍警戒，實際作戰多由各部將領自行決定進退。戰爭的大背景是拜占庭與薩珊的長期戰爭：紅海東岸與也門是兩強角力的走廊，薩珊取得也門控制權後切斷阿克蘇姆通往印度的香料與象牙商路，阿克蘇姆則必須保住自己在也門北岸的據點與教會網絡。雙方的兵力數字都沒有留下可核的記載，只能從阿克蘇姆能同時維持紅海航線與高原攻勢這一點，反推其軍隊相當可觀。
countriesEn: The siege of Sanna was one of the episodes in the struggle between the kingdom of Aksum and Sasanian Persia over Yemen in the late sixth century, and the place of fighting was the capital of the Yemeni highlands, Sanna. The besieging side was the expeditionary army sent out by the kingdom of Aksum (Ethiopia), commanded by Abrahah, a man of noble birth and long military experience. Under him served infantry and cavalry of Aksum itself, Byzantine-style mercenaries in Aksumite pay, the remnants of Himyar, and tribal auxiliaries from Arabia. The chain of command ran from the king's orders and the general's field commands; the camp and the order of battle followed Aksumite practice, which itself carried Roman tradition, with the armoured infantry, the elephants and the tent-lines at the core. The defending side was the Sasanian garrison of Yemen under the Sasanian-appointed governor of the province, with Persian and Arab soldiers, Himyarite levies, and armed members of the Christian and Jewish communities of the city. On the Persian side command followed the satrapic organisation of the Sasanian empire, the governor directing the city defence and the outer pickets, while in practice much of the fighting was left to the individual commanders of the various detachments. The wider background was the long war between Byzantium and Sasanian Persia: the eastern shore of the Red Sea and Yemen were the corridor in which the two powers fought, and after the Sasanians took control of Yemen they cut the route by which Aksum brought ivory and spices out of India, while Aksum had to keep its ports and its network of churches on the northern Yemeni coast. Neither side left a verifiable figure for its numbers; the size of the Aksumite army can only be inferred from the fact that it kept a sea route open while operating a highland offensive at the same time.
people: 核心人物是阿布拉哈。阿拉伯語史料稱他出身阿克蘇姆貴族，能讀寫、懂算學，通曉多種語言，統兵前已歷軍旅，是阿克蘇姆在也門最有經驗的將領之一；關於他的記述全部出自他的敵手，那些阿拉伯編年家雖不得不承認他的才幹，寫法卻多有誇飾，因此留下的形象既失真，又不失其骨幹。他奉王命率軍入也門，先取沿岸要地馬什哈德（al-Mashhad，一說在今日摩卡附近的港塞），再圍沙那，圍城不成遂轉而北上攻擊麥加。薩珊方面最關鍵的人物是也門總督瓦赫里斯（Wahrez）：這位手握軍政大權的波斯將領於570年據沙那起兵反對科斯勞二世，兵敗後逃往阿克蘇姆求助，反而把阿克蘇姆拉進了也門的戰局。與他相對的是薩珊特使馬茲卡（Maz'ka），奉命前往阿克蘇姆朝廷，以財貨與許諾換取阿克蘇姆撤出也門、或轉而與拜占庭為敵；阿拉伯傳統說他攜帶大量金銀並說動了部分人，細節多有誇飾，但可以確定的是，他這趟差事正是沙那圍城戰的直接導火線。阿克蘇姆之王在阿拉伯史料中多未具名，部分學者認為是卡列布（Kaleb，即 Ella Asbeha）或與他同期的一位君主。麥加一端，古爾什部的長老阿布杜·穆塔利卜率代表團迎向象軍，此時約四十歲、出身哈希姆部族的穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉亦參與其事，後世傳統把這一年記作他的出生年，並說他在象軍與朝覲者之間奔走，鼓勵守城。守城方則以沙那總督與其營中軍官為核心，阿拉伯傳統另存有守軍勇士在圍城期間屢挫攻城者的片段。
peopleEn: The central figure is Abrahah. The Arabic sources make him out to be of Aksumite noble birth, literate and skilled in calculation, familiar with several languages, and already a soldier of long standing before he was given command: one of the most experienced commanders Aksum had in Yemen. Everything said about him comes from his enemies, and the Arab chroniclers, though obliged to concede his ability, wrote with a flourish; the portrait that survives is therefore both inflated and, in its substance, sound. He came to Yemen on the king's orders, took the coastal stronghold of al-Mashhad first (identified by some with the port fortress near the modern al-Makha), then laid siege to Sanna, and when the siege failed turned north to strike Mecca. The key figure on the Sasanian side was the governor of Yemen, Wahrez: this general, who held military and civil authority, rose in revolt against Khusrau II at Sanna in 570 and, defeated, fled to the Aksumite court for help, which was precisely what dragged Aksum into the Yemeni war. Against him was the Sasanian envoy Maz'ka, sent to the Aksumite court to buy the kingdom off with money and promises, to persuade it to leave Yemen or to turn against Byzantium instead. The tradition says he carried great quantities of gold and silver and won over part of the court; the details are plainly embellished, but what is certain is that his mission was the immediate spark of the siege of Sanna. The Aksumite king is left unnamed in the Arabic sources; some scholars take him to be Kaleb, that is Ella Asbeha, or a contemporary of his. On the Mecca side the elder of the Quraysh, Abd al-Muttalib, headed a delegation to meet the elephant host, and Muhammad son of Abd Allah, then about forty and of the Hashimite clan, took part as well: later tradition dates his birth to that very year and has him ranging between the host and the pilgrims to encourage the defence. On the defending side the centre was the governor of Sanna together with his officers, and the Arabic tradition preserves a few fragments about defenders who repeatedly checked the besiegers.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬標槍（pilum）並沒有出現在也門的戰場上。它是羅馬軍團的破盾投槍：半米上下的木製槍幹，槍身中空以便飛行時穩定，前端套一段鐵矛頭；投向盾牌時，矛頭會沒入盾面，槍幹隨即彎折留在木盾上，盾兵若不肯放下盾牌便抬不起手臂，於是這一枚小小的投槍便把重裝防禦變成消耗品。把它放進沙那圍城戰的裝備表，是要標出它在體系裡的位置——圍城者最怕的正是城頭的盾牆與居高臨下的箭雨，而壓制城頭正是投槍齊射的傳統功能。實際作戰的是阿克蘇姆與也門的武裝：長矛（希木葉式的長柄矛）、投槍、弓箭——也門弓手在後世記錄中以命中準確著稱——以及手投石與投石索，這種帶皮兜的繩索武器在紅海兩岸的部落中廣泛流傳，便於在碎石遍地的山地上快速拋擲。防護方面是木框蒙皮的小圓盾、鎖子甲與皮革護具，核心部隊另有頭盔與更好的鎗甲。攻城器材包括雲梯、攻城塔與用於掘進的坑道；阿拉伯史料還說阿布拉哈備有攻城機械，並在沙那城郊展開可以移動的攻城塔，塔頂覆以濕牛皮與枝條，防禦方的火箭與投石便不易直接燒毀。野戰力量以馬隊為主，阿克蘇姆騎兵在紅海東岸與拜占庭人交鋒時屢有記載，攻城時則用來包抄與封鎖道路。運輸靠馬、驢、牛與雙峰駱駝，糧食由埃塞俄比亞高原越哈拉茲山脈運入也門高原，這條補給線的長度，正是圍城失敗的真正關鍵。
kitsEn: The Roman pilum on the card did not appear on any battlefield in Yemen. It was the shield-breaking javelin of the Roman legions: a wooden shaft of about half a metre, hollow so that it would fly steadily, with an iron head fitted to the front. Thrown against a shield, the head sank into the face and the shaft bent and stayed in the wood; a man who would not drop his shield could not lift his arm, so that a small javelin turned heavy armour into a consumable. It is placed in the equipment table of the siege of Sanna to mark the position it held in the system, for what the besieger fears most is the shield wall on the rampart and the arrows coming down from above, and suppressing the rampart was the traditional function of a volley of javelins. What actually fought in Yemen were Aksumite and Yemeni weapons: long spears of the Himyarite pattern, throwing javelins, and bows, the Yemeni archers being noted in later records for their accuracy, together with hand-thrown stones and slings, the hide-sling being widely carried by the tribes on both shores of the Red Sea and convenient for quick throwing over stony ground. Protection was the small round shield of wood covered with hide, mail, and leather gear, with helmets and better armour for the core of the troops. The siege equipment included ladders, siege towers and sapping; the Arabic sources also say that Abrahah had siege machines, and that mobile towers were worked against the walls outside Sanna, their tops covered with wet hide and brush so that the defenders' fire-arrows and stones could not easily burn them. Field strength rested mainly on cavalry, Aksumite horse being repeatedly mentioned in fighting on the eastern Red Sea coast, and used in the siege to turn the flank and close the roads. Transport was by horse, donkey, ox and Bactrian camel, and the grain came from the Ethiopian highlands over the Haraz mountains; the length of that supply line was the true hinge on which the siege turned.
tactics: 阿布拉哈的作戰是一套典型的「先取海路、再合圍」的流程。他先以艦隊掩護陸軍在也門北岸上岸，奪取港口要地馬什哈德，切斷沙那與紅海之間的聯繫，然後才把主力壓向高原都城。圍城期間，進攻方在城外環形紮營、掘壕築壘，把營地本身當作前哨；接近沙那必須靠雲梯與攻城塔，因為也門高原的都城依山勢而建，牆基直接坐落在裸露的岩臺之上，攻城器械難以推近。突擊以夜襲為主，趁守軍換班、火把照明不足時攀城；投石與投槍先手清空城頭的射位，再架雲梯。守方則利用城牆的高度，以弓、石與滾木反制，並在夜裡出城襲擊營盤、燒毀攻城器械，同時封鎖城郊道路，試圖拖垮進攻方。進攻方真正的難處不在城牆，而在高原：高海拔使晝夜溫差極大，夜間的寒冷與雨季的泥濘造成大量與戰鬥無關的減員，腹股溝的感染與腳部的潰爛在古代營地是常見傷病；更致命的是距離，埃塞俄比亞的後方基地在紅海彼岸與南方高原，糧秣與援軍的補充必須翻越山脈，圍城拖得越久，這條線便拉得越長。羅馬標槍所在的傳統，在這裡正好可以作為對照：羅馬軍團密集的投槍齊射，就是在城頭盾牆前製造短暫空隙的標準手段；只是沙那的實戰記錄裡，並沒有留下阿克蘇姆人如何射擊的細節。
tacticsEn: Abrahah's method was the classic sequence of taking the sea route first and then closing the ring. He landed the army on the north Yemeni coast under cover of his fleet, seized the port stronghold of al-Mashhad, cut Sanna off from the Red Sea, and only then pressed his main force against the highland capital. During the investment the besiegers camped in a ring round the city, dug trenches and threw up earthworks, treating the camp itself as a forward post. Approaching Sanna required ladders and towers, for the highland capital was built on the lie of the hill and the foot of its wall stood on bare rock, so that siege engines could hardly be brought up. Assaults were made by night, when the watch was changing and the torches of the defenders were not enough to see by; stones and javelins were thrown first to clear the firing positions on the wall, and the ladders were then set up. The defenders answered from the height of the wall with arrows, stones and rolling logs, sallied out by night to strike the camp and burn the siege engines, and closed the roads outside the city in the hope of wearing the besieger down. The besieger's real difficulty lay not in the wall but in the highland: the altitude brought an extreme difference between day and night, and the cold of the night together with the mud of the rains produced a large loss that had nothing to do with fighting, while infected groins and ulcerated feet were ordinary complaints of an ancient camp. More fatal was the distance, for the base in Ethiopia lay across the Red Sea and away to the south, and grain and reinforcements had to cross the mountains; the longer the siege ran, the longer that line grew. The tradition to which the Roman pilum belonged is exactly the right point of comparison here: the dense volley of javelins was the standard means of opening a short gap in a shield wall before ladders were set against it, though the records of Sanna preserve no detail of how the Aksumites actually shot.
data: 可核對的數字不多，且多屬年表與地理。第一，年份：一般把沙那圍城戰繫於公元570年，部分學者定於571年；阿拉伯編年以「象之年」紀年，而回曆始於622年，兩套紀年不能直接換算。第二，地理：沙那位於也門高原，今日市區海拔仍近兩千三百米，是高原上少數可以長久屯兵的大城；舊城牆的現存部分多為晚期重修，不能直接用於570年，該年城牆的高度與周長無可考。第三，距離：由沙那至麥加的直線距離約八百一十公里（依兩地經緯度計算），若沿哈拉茲山脈與沿海提哈馬地帶行軍，實際路程在千公里上下。第四，人數與時長：圍城方與守城的兵力數字都沒有留下，阿克蘇姆軍隊的規模只能從其能同時維持紅海航線與高原攻勢反推；圍城歷時，阿拉伯史料只說「多月」，沒有確數；象的頭數在各種傳述裡分歧很大，不能套用到沙那之戰。第五，可核的物質證據有兩類：錢幣上，六世紀起希木葉銀幣模仿薩珊德拉克姆並加上十字架記號，阿克蘇姆王國也鑄造模仿拜占庭金幣（solidus）的金幣，說明兩國與地中海世界並未隔絕；銘文與遺物上，也門高原的 Musnad 字母王名銘文、薩珊在也門發行的銅幣，與沙那城堡的考古發掘，共同勾勒出六世紀末也門的政治版圖，而亞丁港則在同一條紅海航線上，六十年後阿拉伯人的登陸即由此展開。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, and most of them belong to the chronology and to the geography. First, the date: the siege of Sanna is generally assigned to 570 AD, though some scholars put it in 571; the Arab chronographers date the affair by the Year of the Elephant, and since the Hijri era begins in 622 the two systems cannot simply be converted into one another. Second, the geography: Sanna lies in the Yemeni highlands, the modern city standing at nearly two thousand three hundred metres, one of the few large towns of the highlands where an army could be quartered for long. The surviving walls belong for the most part to later rebuilding and cannot be used for 570, and the height and circuit of the walls in that year are simply unknown. Third, distance: the great-circle distance from Sanna to Mecca is about eight hundred and ten kilometres, computed from the coordinates of the two places, and a march by the Haraz mountains and along the Tihama coastal belt would run to roughly a thousand. Fourth, numbers of men and length of time: no figure survives for either the besieging or the defending force, and the size of the Aksumite army can only be inferred from its having kept a sea route open while operating in the highlands; as for the duration, the Arab sources say only that it lasted several months and give no exact figure; the number of elephants varies widely in the different traditions and cannot be carried over to the siege of Sanna. Fifth, the material evidence falls into two classes. In the coinage, Himyarite silver from the sixth century imitates the Sasanian drachm and adds a cross, and the kingdom of Aksum struck gold in imitation of the Byzantine solidus, which shows that the two realms were not cut off from the Mediterranean world. In inscriptions and objects, the Musnad royal names of the Yemeni highlands, the copper coinage the Sasanians issued in Yemen, and the excavations of the citadel of Sanna together set out the political map of Yemen in the late sixth century; the port of Aden lay on the same Red Sea route, and was to see Arab landings some sixty years later.
cause: 打起來的直接起因，是外交與叛亂交錯在一起。570年，薩珊在也門的總督瓦赫里斯據沙那起兵反對科斯勞二世，兵敗後逃到阿克蘇姆王庭求援；阿克蘇姆本已因薩珊奪取也門、切斷紅海東岸通往印度的香料與象牙商路而懷恨，瓦赫里斯的到來正好提供了開戰的契機與名分。科斯勞二世則派馬茲卡赴阿克蘇姆，用財富與許諾勸說阿克蘇姆放棄也門、或者轉而對付拜占庭；交涉沒有成功，於是阿克蘇姆軍隊改以武力解決：先取港口，再圍沙那。深一層的原因是地緣與商業的結構性衝突。阿克蘇姆王國的主要收入依賴紅海象牙、印度香料以及羅馬與拜占庭的貴金屬貿易，而也門是這條商路在陸地上的轉口點；薩珊控制也門高原，等於同時控制高原的稅收與通往印度的新路，兩國都不可能長期容忍對方站在那裡。第三層是宗教與族群因素：阿克蘇姆在也門北部沿海經營了數百年的基督教教區與商站，面對薩珊省區的收編與皈依政策，其生存感被直接威脅；希木葉殘部與也門基督徒社群夾在兩者之間，多數選擇站在波斯人一方守城。最後一層是時間因素：麥加的朝覲季節商旅雲集，是一年之中麥加城防最薄弱而兵力最集中之時，阿克蘇姆一旦在也門得手，便不會放過這個窗口。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the war was the crossing of diplomacy and rebellion. In 570 the Sasanian governor of Yemen, Wahrez, rose at Sanna against Khusrau II; defeated, he fled to the court of Aksum for help. Aksum had reason enough to be hostile, for the Sasanian seizure of Yemen had cut the Red Sea road by which ivory and Indian spices moved, and the arrival of Wahrez supplied both the opportunity and the justification for a war. Khusrau II sent Maz'ka to the Aksumite court to use money and promises to persuade Aksum to leave Yemen, or to turn against Byzantium instead; the negotiation failed, and the Aksumite army settled the matter by force, taking the ports first and then surrounding Sanna. One layer deeper lies the structural conflict of geography and commerce. The main revenues of the kingdom of Aksum rested on Red Sea ivory, on Indian spices and on the Roman and Byzantine trade in precious metal, and Yemen was the transshipment point of that road on land; while Sasanian control of the Yemeni highlands meant control at once of the highland revenue and of the new road to India, and neither state could long tolerate the other standing there. A third layer is religious and ethnic. Aksum had maintained for centuries a Christian bishopric and a chain of trading stations on the northern Yemeni coast, and its survival was directly threatened by the Sasanian province's policy of incorporation and of conversion; the Himyarite remnant and the Yemeni Christian communities stood between the two powers and for the most part chose to man the walls on the Persian side. The last layer is one of timing: the pilgrimage season filled Mecca with merchants, and it was the moment of the year when the city's defence was weakest while its defenders were most concentrated; once Aksum had its footing in Yemen, it would not forgo that window.
impact: 沙那圍城戰本身的記載稀少，但它在史上的重量來自它所引發的一連串後果。第一，它把阿克蘇姆與薩珊在也門的角力從暗鬥變成公開戰爭，也直接導向翌年的麥加之戰：阿布拉哈在沙那碰壁後轉而北上，企圖在朝覲季節攻入麥加、摧毀卡巴，最終在麥加城外折戟。阿拉伯編年把這場失敗視為神蹟，《古蘭經》第一百零五章〈象軍章〉即為其最精煉的文本；聖訓中又記麥加的「石頭」曾被象血污染、卡巴需要洗刷三次，可見這段記憶在信仰與民間都被長期保存。第二，它成了阿拉伯語世界「統一之前的最後一場共同危機」：據伊本·希沙姆《Sirah》的說法，象之年後古爾什各部族在驚魂未定之中走向和解與結盟；而在那一代成長、數年後開始公開傳教的人物，正是本場戰爭所屬時代的起點。第三，在歐亞尺度上，這場戰爭是拜占庭—薩珊戰爭在紅海東岸的延伸，其後果延伸到東羅馬的海上同盟、薩珊的西邊防線與阿克蘇姆的教會版圖。第四，它在技術與戰史書寫上留下一個範例：高地都城的圍城戰，最先擊垮進攻方的往往不是城牆，而是補給線與氣候，這一點在後世阿拉伯與拜占庭邊境衝突的記述中反覆出現；而羅馬標槍這類破盾投槍，其生命遠比它所屬的帝國更長。
impactEn: The siege of Sanna itself is thinly documented, but its weight in history comes from what it set in motion. First, it turned the Aksumite-Sasanian struggle in Yemen from a concealed contest into open war, and it led directly to the battle of Mecca in the following year: after being checked at Sanna, Abrahah turned north in the hope of entering Mecca during the pilgrimage season and destroying the Kaaba, and he was finally broken outside the walls. The Arab chronographers read that failure as a miracle, and the hundred and fifth sura of the Koran, al-Fiil, is the most compressed statement of it; the hadith further records that the Stone at Mecca was stained with an elephant's blood and that the Kaaba had to be washed three times, which shows how long the memory was kept both in the religious and in the popular register. Second, it became the last common crisis before the unification of Arabia: according to the Sirah of Ibn Hisham, the tribes of the Quraysh, shaken by the Elephant, moved towards reconciliation and alliance; and the man who grew up in that generation and began to preach publicly a few years later is the starting point of the period to which this campaign belongs. Third, on a Eurasian scale the war was the extension of the Byzantine-Sasanian conflict to the eastern shore of the Red Sea, and its consequences reached the maritime alliance of the Eastern Roman empire, the western frontier of the Sasanians, and the ecclesiastical map of Aksum. Fourth, it left an example in technique and in the writing of military history: in the siege of a highland capital, what breaks the besieger is often not the wall but the supply line and the climate, a point that recurs in the later accounts of the Arab and Byzantine frontier wars; and a shield-breaking javelin such as the Roman pilum outlived the empire that made it by a very long way.
result: 沙那沒有陷落。圍城延續數月，阿克蘇姆人始終未能突破城牆，也未能切斷守軍的糧水；攻城塔與雲梯在高原的寒冷與抵抗中一一損毀，薩珊在也門的省區建制得以延續，瓦赫里斯的殘部與其支持者亦未在城破之前被消滅。關於結局，阿拉伯編年的主流說法是圍城失敗，但也有零星異說提到阿克蘇姆軍只取得部分得手便轉兵北上，記錄本身並不足以判定細節。無論如何，阿布拉哈最終被迫撤圍，把軍隊轉向麥加，這一轉向使阿克蘇姆的遠征在麥加城外以失敗收場：象軍沒有攻破麥加，進攻者退回也門，傳統記述則給它安上一個神意的解釋。於是戰果可以這樣概括——阿克蘇姆在沙那沒有拿到它想要的東西：高地都城仍握在薩珊手中，紅海的航權仍在阿克蘇姆手上，邊界大致維持原狀，阿克蘇姆對也門北岸的統治也延續下去。對守方而言，這是一場代價高昂但成色十足的防守；而對雙方而言，這場戰役的真正教訓是：遠征軍在敵國高原上打的最後一仗，往往是在自己的後方完成的。沙那之後的也門，要到七世紀初才被另一支遠征軍——自阿拉伯半島而來的哈里發軍——在阿瓦斯戰役與隨後的攻城中真正拿下，阿克蘇姆在也門數百年的經營方才真正終結。
resultEn: Sanna did not fall. The siege ran for several months; the Aksumites never breached the wall and never cut the defenders off from grain and water; the towers and ladders were destroyed one by one in the cold of the highlands and in the resistance of the defenders; the Sasanian provincial structure in Yemen survived; and the remnants of Wahrez and his supporters were not annihilated before the walls gave way. On the outcome, the mainstream of the Arab narrative has it that the siege failed, though a few stray versions say that the Aksumite army gained only a partial success before turning north, and the records themselves are not enough to settle the detail. Either way Abrahah was finally obliged to lift the siege and turn his army on Mecca, and that turn brought the Aksumite expedition to an end in failure outside the city: the elephant host did not take Mecca, the invaders fell back into Yemen, and the tradition gave the episode a divine explanation. The result can be put in this way. Aksum did not get at Sanna what it wanted: the highland capital stayed in Sasanian hands, the shipping of the Red Sea stayed in Aksumite hands, the frontier remained roughly where it was, and Aksumite rule over the north Yemeni coast continued. For the defenders this was a costly but creditable defence; and for both sides the true lesson of the campaign is that the last battle of a distant army on a foreign highland is often fought on its own rear. Yemen after Sanna was not taken until the early seventh century by another distant army, the caliphal force that came from the Arabian peninsula, in the battle of Awtas and the sieges that followed; only then did the long Aksumite tenure of Yemen come to an end.
